title: Build an Idempotent ETL Pipeline
summary: Extract a messy CSV export, clean and validate it, deduplicate to the latest version of each record, and upsert it into a warehouse table so re-runs never duplicate data.

hints.test_extract_handles_quotes_and_whitespa: Use csv.DictReader over io.StringIO(text). It understands quoted fields that contain commas. Strip whitespace from keys and values.
hints.test_transform_normalizes_fields: Lower-case and strip emails, upper-case country codes, convert amount to float and dates to ISO 'YYYY-MM-DD'.
hints.test_transform_parses_both_date_formats: Try datetime.strptime with '%Y-%m-%d' and then '%d/%m/%Y', and format the result with .date().isoformat().
hints.test_transform_rejects_bad_rows_with_rea: Never drop rows silently. Put them in rejects as {**row, 'reason': '...'} and keep going.
hints.test_transform_keeps_latest_version_per_: Group by order_id and keep the row with the greatest updated_at. ISO timestamps compare correctly as strings.
hints.test_load_creates_table_and_upserts: CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS with order_id as PRIMARY KEY, then INSERT … ON CONFLICT(order_id) DO UPDATE SET … = excluded.….
hints.test_pipeline_is_idempotent: Running the same file twice must leave exactly the same table. Upserts, not plain INSERTs, make that true.
hints.test_rerun_applies_corrections: When a newer extract changes an order's amount, the upsert must overwrite the old value.
hints.test_pipeline_metrics: Return counts for each stage, so a run can be audited: extracted = rows read, loaded = rows upserted, rejected = rows rejected.
